data.narrative:
Quindar is a Series A-stage space and aerospace company founded by Matthew Regan, Zach Meza, David Lawrence, Sandilya Bhagavathula, Shaishav Parekh, and Nate Hamet. The company has raised $27.3M to date. The relevant peer universe includes 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) with a median P/S multiple of 27.4x, and 8 private-stage peers in the Space & Aerospace sector, including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised ($27.3M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage transitions yields an implied valuation of $55M. This reflects typical investor expectations for value creation between financing rounds in this sector.

The peer-median and public-comp anchoring methods are not applicable. Insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage private peers meeting tight filtering criteria (0 to 2 matches against a minimum of 3 required) preclude reliable peer-set median derivation. Public-comp anchoring cannot proceed due to the absence of revenue data for Quindar—a constraint endemic to private companies. The analysis therefore supports a valuation range of $46M to $63M, centered on $55M, reflecting the stage-progression methodology. Key uncertainties include revenue trajectory, customer traction, and the company's differentiation within a crowded frontier-aerospace landscape.
